findings.exposure: Public in-memory UMAP/PCA; default sizes/workloads determine exposure.
findings.qualification: F/R depend on reciprocity/pruning; staging/sort slack and ARC lifetimes vary. This is a byte model, not measured RSS. In-memory design explicitly documented.

findings.claim: Graph sorts/epoch scans and PCA per-point transforms offer concrete allocation/work opportunities.
findings.exposure: Public synchronous algorithms; no throughput regression measured.
findings.qualification: Not missing ANN/GPU functionality; serial deterministic and in-memory contract is explicit.

findings.claim: Long synchronous manifold/factorization work lacks cancellation checkpoints.
findings.exposure: Callers using synchronous APIs, including inside async tasks.
findings.qualification: No broken cancellation guarantee is documented. Large positive powerIterations requests more work intentionally.

findings.claim: C INT8 accumulation can exceed signed32 range only beyond supported fixed-vector dimensions.
findings.exposure: Generic exported C lanes API; optional Swift C INT8 call sites use fixed512/768/1536.
findings.qualification: Do not allege active fixed-width overflow. C intrinsic lane behavior differs from scalar C signed-overflow language semantics; no Intel/NEON overflow execution or UBSan run.

findings.claim: C header range indexing wording and proposed unimplemented declarations need precise public status.
findings.exposure: Public C/header and Swift wrapper interface; no current Swift link failure established.
findings.qualification: Header declaration of proposed symbol is API-hygiene risk, not proof a normal build fails.

findings.claim: Allocation-heavy vector helpers, unequal SIMD reduction structure and platform heuristics warrant measurement, not speed claims.
findings.exposure: Public VectorMath helpers; internal PlatformConfiguration and mostly unused optimization helpers.
findings.qualification: No universal measured slowdown; no illegal instruction dispatch is proven from these width/cache hints.

findings.claim: LAPACK dimension ceiling does not by itself establish extreme workspace arithmetic safety.
findings.exposure: Shapes far beyond documented small-panel operating envelope.
findings.qualification: Do not elevate to verified practical memory-corruption defect. Two Int32 dimensions multiply safely in64-bit Swift Int; workspace arithmetic is distinct.

findings.claim: Public DynamicVector and optimized FP32 storage mutations break shape invariants.
findings.exposure: public default representations
findings.qualification: Do not say every vector or every check fails: generic Vector<D> uses a count-constrained DimensionStorage; FP16 conversions explicitly check malformed FP32 storage. No out-of-bounds write was executed. Different hash values are an observed consequence, not a mathematical guarantee against incidental hash collisions.

findings.claim: INT8 raw constructors, mutable storage, and synthesized Codable permit malformed fixed storage.
findings.exposure: public opt-in INT8 APIs
findings.qualification: FP16 vectors are immutable and exact-length validated; they are not part of this shape defect. Invalid INT8 storage is observed; resulting unsafe reads are source-derived, not an executed memory fault. Synthesized decoding bypasses any future initializer-only fix.

findings.claim: NormalizationHint retains metadata after direct wrapped mutation or a throwing mutable-buffer closure.
findings.exposure: public wrapper; inspected downstream consumers
findings.qualification: The initial hint is true, so this is not caller supplying a false assertion. GPU/downstream end-to-end behavior was not executed; existing contaminated indexes needing rebuild is conditional, not established deployment state.

findings.claim: SoAFP16Cache512 treats vector hash digests as exact candidate identity.
findings.exposure: public opt-in cache; no default or sibling caller found
findings.qualification: Only the512 cache exists; 384/768/1536 key initializers are currently unused future surface. Full-coordinate hashing alone cannot turn a digest into an equality proof.

findings.claim: Compact-tier triangular matrix copies share later mutations.
findings.exposure: public TriangularMatrix default sizes4...32; internal compact counts5...512
findings.qualification: Range is derived from m=n(n-1)/2; no claim for an arbitrary configured tier. Iterator snapshot and setAt exposure follow their same stored-copy/setter paths, not independent runtime reproduction.

findings.claim: Binary in-place DynamicVector routes omit dimension checks.
findings.exposure: public direct defaults and generic VectorProtocol operator dispatch
findings.qualification: Do not extend unchecked dispatch claim to concrete VectorFactory +=, which checks through +. Short RHS optimized overread is static reasoning; no Release overread was intentionally executed.

findings.claim: Optimized-vector hashes omit all but first and last eight scalar values.
findings.exposure: all four public optimized vector types; no vector-keyed downstream table found
findings.qualification: Legal Hashable collisions are a scaling issue, not equal-values-have-equal-hash violation. O(N^2*d) is worst-case equality work for sufficiently late differences, not measured universal cost. SIMD signed zero is not an additional bug.

findings.claim: Pointer normalization documents16-byte alignment as preferred but SIMD loads require it.
findings.exposure: public NormalizeKernels.normalizeUnchecked pointer overload
findings.qualification: Report Debug trap and source alignment precondition violation, not a reproduced Release failure. Dimension<4 does not enter SIMD loads. Caller meets documented Float capacity/nonzero magnitude obligations.

findings.claim: Vector384Optimized permanently rebinds typed-owner memory where other widths restore binding.
findings.exposure: normal public construction/toArray/buffer access
findings.qualification: Keep as binding-lifetime maintenance/contract finding. Layout compatibility is not a blanket strict-aliasing exemption; conversely merely seeing different spellings does not prove an observed miscompile. Alignment of Float-array source must be audited separately across all widths.

findings.claim: Compact generic storage does not destroy manually initialized ManagedBuffer tail elements.
findings.exposure: public TriangularMatrix<T>, default compact sizes4...32
findings.qualification: Reference-bearing arrays/strings follow missing generic destruction by source; only class sentinel was executed. A ManagedBuffer frees allocation but does not implicitly destroy manually initialized elements.

findings.claim: alignedCopy has incompatible initialize versus update semantics across alignment branches.
findings.exposure: public generic utility; no production caller found
findings.qualification: This is an unsafe API contract gap, not proof of a fault under a clearly documented supported destination state (none is supplied). Uninitialized-destination crash was not executed. Alignment here means preferred64-byte alignment, not natural-type misalignment.

findings.claim: HybridStorage repeating construction/fill performs quadratic buffer traffic.
findings.exposure: DynamicVector repeating/fill/resize above16 Float elements; explicit hybrid heap storage
findings.qualification: Exact count1026 belongs to the instrumented fixture; actual Release instruction path independently proves duplicated ownership/copying and quadratic element traffic. Pointer addresses staying unchanged after writes do not refute copying: two replacement allocations can reuse prior address. SIMD stubs are not used to claim numerical results. Generic DimensionStorage default heap mutation does not inherit this finding.

findings.claim: TriangularMatrix scalar writes copy complete standard/aligned allocations even when uniquely owned.
findings.exposure: public default matrix n>=33; original emphasized aligned n>=65
findings.qualification: Extend original exposure: standard tier513...2048 also detaches on scalar mutation, so repairing only AlignedBuffer.isUniquelyReferenced is insufficient. Address-change evidence uses integer addresses outside borrow scopes, not retained storage copies.

findings.claim: Dormant TieredStorage bulk access loses standard writes and inline writes on thrown closure exit.
findings.exposure: internal dormant mutable-buffer route; no production caller found
findings.qualification: No current public matrix method routes through this bulk method. It becomes a required dependency if the proposed matrix bulk-fill optimization is introduced.

findings.claim: Internal StorageSlice returns scoped pointer without keeping its owner alive.
findings.exposure: internal dormant APIs; no production call found
findings.qualification: No supported-use UAF executed. This is distinct from DynamicVector.slice, which returns an owned vector.

findings.claim: Experimental consuming into() returns memory still freed by deinit.
findings.exposure: internal compile gate MOVE_ONLY_EXPERIMENTAL absent from package settings
findings.qualification: Not compiled in ordinary builds and not runtime-reproduced. Do not enable this gate as an optimization without rederiving all lifetime paths.

findings.claim: Public FP16 pointer getters escape ContiguousArray borrow scopes.
findings.exposure: public opt-in fp16Storage getters; kernels use scoped borrows
findings.qualification: The getter is explicitly unsafe; do not equate pointer return with a demonstrated supported-use corruption. Retaining the array owner alone does not change the documented nonescape condition of withUnsafeBufferPointer.

findings.claim: SoAFP16Cache512 accepts nonpositive maxSize then evicts from an empty list.
findings.exposure: public explicit cache configuration; default100 unaffected
findings.qualification: Lower priority configuration boundary. Choose whether zero intentionally disables caching before testing desired policy.

findings.claim: FP16 cache caps entry count while payload bytes scale with candidates per entry.
findings.exposure: public opt-in512 cache
findings.qualification: Sizing derivation, not attempted allocation/RSS measurement; immutable COW cache values are not themselves an actor data race.

findings.claim: StaticDimension.Storage customization is unused by Vector<D> storage yet controls extension availability.
findings.exposure: public custom dimensions
findings.qualification: Confusing customization/API gating, not demonstrated numerical failure.

findings.claim: VectorTypeFactory optimized wording describes generic fixed-vector selection, not specialized concrete types.
findings.exposure: public factory
findings.qualification: No measured performance regression. Changing the output type can alter casts, provider routing and generic overload behavior.

findings.claim: VectorCoreOperations creates redundant arrays and temporary results.
findings.exposure: public min/max/clamp operations
findings.qualification: Source-visible allocation opportunities; no measured regression or speedup. Constructor cost can additionally be affected by HybridStorage finding.

findings.claim: Performance/robustness comments exceed evidence and overlapping storage layers obscure actual ownership.
findings.exposure: public docs and maintainers
findings.qualification: General consolidation is an opportunity, not authorization for a wholesale rewrite or proof of universal slowness. Norm arithmetic validation belongs numerical reviewer.

findings.claim: SoA/page/raw ownership, size and custom-conformer obligations are already documented.
findings.exposure: unsafe borrowed/transfer/custom conformer surfaces
findings.qualification: No additional supported-use corruption established from missing post-transfer checks, @unchecked Sendable, or ordinary checked arithmetic trapping on invalid/oversized shapes. Four built-in layouts do not prove arbitrary custom conformers.

findings.claim: AlignedDynamicArrayStorage fallback can weaken alignment while guaranteedAlignment reports the request.
findings.exposure: public allocation-failure fallback
findings.qualification: Keep a potential guarantee gap, not reproduced misalignment or corruption.

findings.claim: Reject extending HybridStorage quadratic-copy behavior to default generic DimensionStorage without evidence.
findings.exposure: generic Vector<D> default storage; explicit .hybrid separately exposed
findings.qualification: Reject blanket claim that linspace/range/generate/geometric/sparse necessarily become quadratic for every generic fixed vector. Explicit .hybrid mode and Double inline threshold deserve dedicated coverage.

findings.claim: Extension-only protocol methods select static defaults in generic code.
findings.exposure: public generic VectorProtocol consumers
findings.qualification: This alone is not a measured performance defect and does not mean all extensions are wrong. Split narrow read-only protocols only where consumer needs justify change.

findings.claim: A valid empty DynamicVector binary encoding cannot be decoded by its own type.
findings.exposure: Public binary round trip of default/empty dynamic values.
findings.qualification: The 10001 cap is a distinct intentionally tested limitation. Do not remove decoder limits as an incidental repair.

findings.claim: Serialization tests include 15 comment-only bodies and mislabeled optimized-type coverage.
findings.exposure: Confidence in passing tests.
findings.qualification: This does not mean all optimized Codable code is untested elsewhere, or that Core should implement every feature mentioned by a placeholder.

findings.claim: Binary conversion has scalar loops and temporary representations; a Release allocation speedup is not yet established.
findings.exposure: Binary encode/decode.
findings.qualification: Retain only a profiling candidate. Neither one heap allocation per scalar in Release nor a throughput regression was demonstrated; do not blindly replace the implementation.

findings.claim: Binary and JSON representations have different type/precision contracts.
findings.exposure: Serialization of optimized FP32 and quantized vectors.
findings.qualification: No compressed-INT8 binary or universal JSON schema promise found. These are documentation/interoperability decisions, not demonstrated corrupt roundtrips.

findings.claim: Vectors expose binary methods without adopting the public binary protocols.
findings.exposure: Generic BinaryCodable integrations; no internal dependent caller found.
findings.qualification: An integration opportunity; no existing downstream generic BinaryCodable compilation failure was claimed.

findings.claim: Header documentation describes VECT while the actual little-endian wire bytes spell TCEV.
findings.exposure: External binary readers/documentation.
findings.qualification: Existing encoder and decoder agree and tests expect actual bytes. This is a documentation defect; changing wire bytes would be a compatibility change.

findings.claim: Decoder framing/CRC bounds and Data-slice behavior support the original limited positive assessment.
findings.exposure: Public binary decoder; context/guardrails, not an additional defect.
findings.qualification: No public overflow exploit, compression implementation defect or direct-slice bug found. CRC is integrity checking, not authentication. Reserved flags are read but unused; one uncompressed frame is the current contract.

findings.claim: Decoded INT8 storage, quantization parameters and TopK result arrays require invariant validation.
findings.exposure: Synthesized/custom Codable construction boundaries.
findings.qualification: Cross-reference OWN/NUM/API rows for severity and actual effects; this row is boundary coverage, not a separate issue count.

findings.claim: Strict benchmark correctness accepts nonfinite errors, mismatched output lengths and missing validation.
findings.exposure: Benchmark CLI; undermines validation of later optimizations.
findings.qualification: NaN JSON failure is separate from threshold acceptance. There was no injected faulty production kernel. This is a validation blocker, not a claim every benchmark value is wrong.

findings.claim: Requested benchmark output can fail to write while the CLI exits successfully.
findings.exposure: Benchmark automation.
findings.qualification: The CLI experiment used a filesystem error; NaN-to-CLI exit behavior follows the same catch/control flow.

findings.claim: Benchmark metadata claims Release/C/size settings that do not establish the binary executed.
findings.exposure: Debug and Release CLI metadata; provenance.
findings.qualification: Requested flags are not proof a C kernel actually ran. No separately compiled C-on/C-off A/B performance measurement was made.

findings.claim: Extended mixed-precision tests bypass the strict-performance opt-out.
findings.exposure: Manual benchmarks workflow with EXTENDED=1, STRICT_PERF=0.
findings.qualification: No current hosted failure or compiler elimination was observed; universal speedup/dimension-order expectations are unsupported by numerical correctness.

findings.claim: Selecting optimized-only dot cases runs zero cases and succeeds.
findings.exposure: Targeted benchmark selection.
findings.qualification: This is case selection/coverage loss, not a zero-duration optimized speedup.

findings.claim: Fused/pre-normalized cosine A/B pairs cannot join under their current grouping keys.
findings.exposure: JSON and console A/B reporting.
findings.qualification: Euclidean pairing is a separate path and is not invalidated by this proof.

findings.claim: Several timings lack consistent result consumption and compare different setup/allocation boundaries.
findings.exposure: Benchmark/test timing paths.
findings.qualification: Missing consumption is proved; dead-code elimination and its timing magnitude are unverified. Different timing scopes can be intentional but must be identified before attributing speedups.

findings.claim: Memory-footprint output counts owning struct handles rather than heap payload.
findings.exposure: Mixed-precision footprint report and misleading timing-test names.
findings.qualification: No allocated-byte or RSS measurement was made; payload arithmetic excludes headers, allocator overhead and COW sharing.

findings.claim: Matrix benchmark ignores shared selection/timing controls and has only 17 distinct generated vectors.
findings.exposure: Opt-in matrix benchmark.
findings.qualification: No claim that 17 distinct vectors makes numerical computation incorrect; it limits representativeness and provenance.

findings.claim: Current benchmark coverage does not establish downstream large-scale behavior.
findings.exposure: Scale-readiness validation gap; no universal throughput claim supported.
findings.qualification: These are coverage opportunities, not proof of a current production outage or a demand to put all workloads into every PR job.

findings.claim: CI coverage excludes important tooling and selected safety surfaces.
findings.exposure: Test/lint/CI configuration.
findings.qualification: No remote branch-protection settings inspected; independent checks may be required externally. Declared analyzer rules alone do not execute analysis. Do not count unregistered tests as coverage.

findings.claim: Baseline comparison ignores provenance and CSV metadata does not escape multiline/arbitrary values.
findings.exposure: Benchmark artifact comparison/export.
findings.qualification: Historical baselines are useful records, not current guarantees. Aggregate means versus medians are choices needing explicit labeling, not inherently arithmetic errors.

findings.claim: Mobile availability of the separate benchmarking product remains unverified.
findings.exposure: VectorCoreBenchmarking product only.
findings.qualification: Do not report a confirmed mobile compile failure or extend this suspicion to the Core product.
